title: Whole Turkey (frozen)

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in the target week. Recent weeks show no consistent trend; back-to-school season ended 2026-08-24. Past promotions had high variance and noise-adjusted effects near baseline. Labor Day had no prior clean occurrence. The classical uplift model correctly suggests no effect. Baseline uncertainty (112% noise) dominates. No driver justifies a multiplier away from 1.0.

brief:

  shelf price: 29.20 (+0.0% vs regular price 29.20)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.0 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 14.9 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-112% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
